name: browser-login-secret-source
description:
The headline Phase C proof: a credentialed sign-in driven through the REAL browser driver end to end — the filler fills a stored login with no secret reaching the model, acting is gated on a web_host#act plan-gate slot, ONE approval covers the whole acting phase, and the run reaches a cookie-gated protected page.

THE SITE IS STATEFUL (test/testbrowser.ServeLoginSite, selected by this bundle's LOGIN_SITE marker): GET / is a real sign-in form; POST /signin checks the credentials, sets a session cookie, and 303-redirects to /protected; /protected shows PROTECTED-CONTENT-SIGNED-IN only WITH that cookie. So reaching the sentinel proves the credentialed round trip actually happened, not that a scripted reply said so.

THE CREDENTIAL NEVER REACHES THE MODEL. The two web_type calls carry {{login.host.docker.internal.username}} / {{login.host.docker.internal.password}} placeholders; the filler substitutes the real values strictly inside the type tool's Execute, AFTER the loop recorded the raw placeholder args. The fixture password is "s3cr3t-fixture" (test/testbrowser.LoginPassword) and lastToolResultNotContains pins it absent from every type result, the protected-page read, and agentReplyNotContains pins it absent from the delivered reply. The type result is a bare "typed into ref eN" status — never the value.

ONE APPROVAL, MANY ACTING CALLS (the carried C3 durability check). The acting sequence makes FOUR web_host#act calls on the same host — type username, type password, click submit, then click Continue on the protected page — and approvalPrompts is 1: the single plan-gate card that approves the signin phase binds the web_host slot, and every acting call after it runs on that grant. A regression that re-prompted per call would auto-approve (tool_approval is in autoApprove deliberately) and surface here as a count of 2+, not a hang. planGate.approvalPrompts:1 and the recorded authz decision web_host:host=2Edocker=2Einternal#act = allowed are the airtight form: the escaped host id is C-R4's chain (spicedb_escape, dots are illegal in a SpiceDB object id), and an allow could only have come from the slot grant the approval wrote — this fixture ships no owner tuple for web_host.

The AgentClass REFERENCES the toolbox (spec.browserToolboxes) — mandatory, because a web_host slot can only be declared by a referencing class (pkg/controllers/agentclass/browser_slot.go). That makes the operator stand up a per-session browser pod and hold the runner until it is Ready; the e2e harness fakes that readiness (no kubelet in envtest) and the reconciler resolves the login catalog from the directCredentials `secret` identity itself.

Everything is asserted on the TOOL RESULT, never the reply.

PHASE D PROOF: the single web_host#act plan-gate card this run publishes also carries a redacted page screenshot. The e2e in-process Loop now wires a real client.Client (test/e2e/inprocess_runner_factory.go, scoped to this one consumer — see its comment there for why it does not also turn on MCP-UI widget persistence), so storeScreenshotArtifact can actually Create the ArtifactRender{Kind:"image"} CR instead of failing closed to text-only. approvalScreenshotAttached asserts the published interaction_request's Screenshot.RenderName is non-empty — proving the capture→redact→store→attach path ran for real against the live browser session behind this sign-in, not just that the unit/integration tests for each stage pass in isolation.
